column1: The item offered in the deal (e.g. egg, coins, potion)
column2: How much cheaper the item is vs its normal shop price
column3: What the player pays in gems to buy this deal
column4: The list of slot numbers (1–6) where this item is permitted to appear
column7: The internal name of the slot being configured (dailyDeals_slot_X_base)
column8: Minimum gem price for an item to appear in this deal position
column9: Maximum gem price — above this, the item is too expensive for this position
column10: Target % of pet upgrade offers in this position (0 = none, 100 = only pets)
column14: Selection frequency: higher = this offer appears more often than others in the same position
column15: how many units the player receives (e.g. 300 coins, 2 potions)
column16: REWARDED (free after watching an ad) or CURRENCY (paid with in-game currency)
column17: How the player pays: gems, coins, or by watching an ad
column19: Calculated gem value of this specific offer (used for the range check)
column20: the calculated Hard Currency equivalent of this specific offer
column21: ✅ TRUE = the offer price fits this position's budget. ❌ FALSE = the price is out of range and must be corrected
column22: the intended share of this item type within the slot (e.g. 33% = 1 in 3 picks)
column23: Total number of item entries competing in this slot's random draw
column26: The deal position this row belongs to
column28: The item shown to the player when this entry is selected
column30: Actual selection frequency used in the calculation (may be overridden)
column31: Real probability (%) that this exact offer appears in the daily deal
column34: the final price combining quantity and currency, as it would appear in the UI
column37: Unlock condition: this deal only appears once the player has reached a specific world

column10: ~Perventage of shards in the offer slot

column7: This part is an auto-weight attributor for shards. You can activate it or not. If not, the "~Weight" column will be used.

column9: "What is the most frequent value ?" 0 is the lowest value, 1 is the highest value
"How well distributed the values are going to be" 0 is all the values are concentrated at the center, 1000 is all the values are equal
